newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RESEARCH ALERT - Were rates Email a buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Were rates Email a buy.

text.p: Melbourne brokerage J.B. Were and Son said it was recommending whitegoods, metals and building and industrial products group Email Ltd as a buy, reflecting the benefits of an improving Australian economy.

"With its exposure to housing, reliance on the domestic economy and leverage to increased volumes in the major appliances and building products divisions, Email should be a prime beneficiary of the Reserve Bank's move to a pro-growth bias," the Were report said.

Were said that at current levels, Email stock was trading at a slight premium to the market based on the broker's estimates for 1997 and was supported by a fully franked sustainable yield of nearly seven percent.
"We believe the stock is attractively priced at these levels, given the evidence that a turnaround in earnings in many of the group's divisions has commenced," the report said.

The report said Were believed Email's strategy of divesting many of its non-core businesses to concentrate on building the strength of its core divisions was the correct one, with the potential for further divestments in the medium term.
"This should enable returns across the firm to improve, and leave the company well placed to benefit from any cyclical recovery," the report said.
Were said the poor short term earnings outlook for the company appeared to be already factored into its share price.
In June, Email posted a net profit of A$55.14 million for the year to March 31, 1996 which was 45 percent lower than the previous year.
The company said it had budgeted for an improved performance in the year to March 31, 1997.
At 2.00 p.m. (0400 GMT), Email shares were two cents weaker at A$3.18.
At the time the Were report was written, Email shares were trading at A$3.26.
